$description: Dreamari design tokens — W3C Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) format. Reverse-engineered directly from the live codebase (src/components/flow/**, src/app/globals.css) as of 2026-08-01, not from the Figma library — Figma is being brought into alignment with this file, not the other way around. Every raw value below was either copied from globals.css or extracted from actual rendered output (Tailwind's stock OKLCH palette entries were converted to hex via canvas pixel sampling in a live browser, not hand-converted, so they are exact). Aliases use the standard DTCG '{group.path}' syntax.

brand.$description: The Brand Kit — the one color family that must stay byte-identical between code and Figma. Sourced from globals.css --color-brand-*. Note the scale has gaps (no 50, no 800) because code never defined them; fill those in only if a real use case appears, don't invent placeholder values.

600.$description: Primary brand blue. Used as the default/fallback accent and the Welcome/Congratulations bookend color.

neutral.$description: The slate/gray scale used for all body text, borders, and neutral surfaces. Shades 500/600/900 are code-defined (globals.css) and intentionally on-brand. Shades 100/200/300/400/700/800 are NOT overridden in code today — they silently fall back to Tailwind v4's stock default slate palette. Values below for those shades were measured directly from rendered output (Tailwind v4 stores its defaults in OKLCH, not hex) so this group is complete and exact, but flagged: decide whether 100/200/300/400/700/800 should stay as generic Tailwind defaults or get their own on-brand values — that's a real open decision, not something this export should silently resolve.

100.$description: Inherited from Tailwind default — not brand-tuned.

200.$description: Inherited from Tailwind default — not brand-tuned.

300.$description: Inherited from Tailwind default — not brand-tuned.

400.$description: Inherited from Tailwind default — not brand-tuned.

700.$description: Inherited from Tailwind default — not brand-tuned.

800.$description: Inherited from Tailwind default — not brand-tuned.

900.$description: Code-defined, on-brand (globals.css --color-slate-900). Primary heading text color.

amber.$description: Renamed vs. the raw CSS variable names in code: globals.css calls the #fef3c7 shade 'amber-100', but its actual value matches the standard amber-50 position on both Tailwind's and Figma's own amber scale. Corrected here since this is a labeling bug, not a deliberate choice — code's variable name should eventually be renamed to match.

600.$description: Used for Future Values / Academic Journey step accents, and matches Figma's colors/amber/600 exactly.

navy.$description: Same naming issue as amber: globals.css calls this shade 'navy-975', Figma's own token calls the identical value 'navy/900'. Corrected here.

accent.$description: Two extra accent colors defined in globals.css with no clear current usage found in src/components/flow — flagged for the dev to confirm still in use before porting.

ink.$description: Defined in globals.css (--color-ink-100/200/900) but no confirmed usage found in src/components/flow during this audit — likely legacy. Flagged, not necessarily broken.

emerald.$description: Stock Tailwind emerald shades used directly in a handful of places (e.g. selected-state greens) with no on-brand override — same situation as the untuned neutral shades. A real candidate for a proper 'success' semantic color once form validation states are designed (Figma's Components library has success/danger/warning tokens that don't exist in code yet at all — not included here since this export is strictly code-derived).

category.$description: The 5 Match Experience card-category hues (matchData.ts MATCH_CARD_META). Blue and amber are aliases to existing brand/amber primitives — only red/purple/green are genuinely new primitives.

blue.$description: Skills card — same as brand blue.

decorative.$description: Ambient/background-only colors found in the aurora background system (stars, blobs, gradients) — not part of the core UI kit. Grouped generically here rather than guessing confident semantic names; a designer should pass over this group specifically and assign real names before it's treated as a stable API.

semantic.$description: Intent-named aliases — this is the layer components should actually consume, never the primitives above directly. This is a representative slice (text/surface/border), not exhaustive; extend once this shape is approved.

secondary.$description: globals.css --color-surface-tertiary, despite the name — worth renaming to 'secondary' for consistency once touched.

default.$description: Static fallback accent — used by the Match Experience phase (MATCH_ACCENT) which isn't one of the 12 rotating Build-step accents.

step-theme.$description: The rotating per-Build-step accent system (src/components/flow/types.ts STEP_AURORA_ACCENTS + FlowContainer's derived gradient stops) — the single biggest thing the old Figma Components library has no concept of at all. 12 modes, one per Build step (1-indexed to match TOTAL_STEPS). 'button-to'/'progress-to' are computed at runtime via CSS color-mix(in srgb, accent 65%, black) unless a step has an explicit override (step 8 only, matched to a specific Figma node per a code comment) — resolved to literal hex here for portability to platforms without color-mix() (e.g. React Native), with the source formula noted per-step.

5.$description: Confidence Check — red, matches its Ronaldo gif

6.$description: Spend Your Days — reuses Academic Journey's teal

button-from.$description: Explicit override, not derived — matched to Figma node 588:35961

8.$description: Future Values — amber, closest to yellow, matches its SpongeBob gif. Only step with an explicit non-derived gradient.

dimension.$description: Spacing/radius/font-size scales. Unlike color, these are already reasonably systematic in code — every value below is one already in real use (Tailwind's own numeric scale), not an invented one. The exceptions are called out explicitly under 'outliers'.

spacing.$description: Keyed by literal pixel value (not Tailwind's internal 1/1.5/2/2.5 numbering) — a dotted key like '2.5' would collide with DTCG's own '{a.b.c}' alias path syntax, and a raw px number needs no Tailwind knowledge to read.

outliers.$description: Arbitrary one-off values found only in MatchCard — not on the scale above. Decide whether to fold these into a formal step, or keep as deliberate one-offs.
MatchCard-only arbitrary sizes, not on the scale above.

component.$description: Component-scoped tokens — the layer components should actually reference in code (never primitives or semantics directly). This is a representative slice covering 3 components to establish the pattern; the remaining ~15 flow components (PathOption, RadioPillGroup, LabeledInput, LabeledSelect, FlowCard, StepHeader, FlowProgress, MatchDeck, ...) follow the identical shape and should be added once this structure is approved.

button.$description: FlowButton — currently a single full-width gradient CTA variant in code (Figma's Components library specs 45: 5 styles x 3 sizes x 3 states, none of which exist yet). Only documenting what's real.

bg-from.$description: Actually dynamic per-step — see color.step-theme. This is just the Welcome-step example value.

selection-item.$description: Covers GridOption + SelectionRow — Figma's 'Selection List Item' equivalent. The two components currently use slightly different padding at the mobile tier (12px vs 14px) — flagged as a real inconsistency between two components meant to be the same concept, not a deliberate design choice.

padding-mobile.$description: GridOption uses 14px; SelectionRow uses 12px (spacing.12) — pick one.

selected-bg.$description: Dynamic per-step via var(--step-accent) — not a fixed color today. Figma's own 'Selection Chip' spec uses a fixed green here instead; noting the divergence, not resolving it.
